utterances.text: We'll come to that, sir. For the moment I'd just asked you how many times you were at the school and I'd ask you to, just so we can move through this most efficiently, to just focus on the question, please. So with that I'd ask you to just refer a few of your positions.

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In 1991, you were named the minister of industry in the SAO Romanija; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was appointed minister of industry in the SAO Romanija. Let me just say that it convened only once. That was a constitutive meeting and it never met again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, just answer the question. There seems to be a sigh. There must be something wrong at this moment because we hear the personal conversation within the booth rather than ...

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Apologies, but it's the button.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I thought it would be. Witness, could you please answer the question and leave it to that. You were appointed or named minister of industry isn't the SAO Krajina. The simple answer is yes -- Romanija. Next question. So would you please strictly limit yourself --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You also served as a member of the Rogatica Crisis Staff; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In May and June 1992, the Crisis Staff was headquartered in the Sladara malt-factory; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Approximately how often, once a day, once a week, several times a week, would you be present at the Sladara malt-factory at that time? And if you're not sure, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, maybe I went there once a week. Not more than that during a week.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You also served as a secretary of the secretariat for national defence in Rogatica; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Rogatica had a multiethnic municipal assembly elected at the multi-party elections in 1990; right? And I see you're nodding but you have to articulate your answer.

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that was a multiparty, multinational assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It also had a Serb assembly established in December 1991; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was formed as a result of the division of the municipal territory and the Muslim authority and the Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, actually --

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is when the assembly was established.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- sir, as a matter of chronology, the agreement on dividing the territory was entered into on the 2nd of May 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is when this decision was adopted at the joint assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, in fact, the Serb assembly was established in December 1991; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you served as a member of both assemblies; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a president of Executive Committee during the tenure of the first assembly. I wasn't a deputy. However, I was a deputy in the Serbian assembly and by replacing someone I became a deputy in the assembly of the Serbian people.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you were also a member of the SDS Municipal Board in Rogatica; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, in late March 1992 you, Sveto Veselinovic, and Tomislav Batinic resigned from the Municipal Board; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was the president of the Executive Committee, Batinic was --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: -- slowly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the interpreters could not catch your words. That's how it is. You resigned in late March 1992 together with Veselinovic and Batinic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was the question. That was the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that is your answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President. Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 31325.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, since you are now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- entering the domain of documents, it's also about time for a break. If you would say it would be better to start with the documents after the break, having introduced the positions of the witness until now, then we would follow that suggestion.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'll follow your suggestion to suggest it, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Witness, we'll take a break of 20 minutes and we would like to see you back after that. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at 20 minutes past midday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ujic, Mr. Traldi will now continue his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, before the break you testified that you, Mr. Veselinovic, and Mr. Batinic had resigned your positions in the Rogatica SDS. What we see now on the screen is the letter you sent to Dr. Karadzic conveying your resignation; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you were informing President Karadzic because the structure of the SDS was that the Municipal Board reported up to the Main Board; correct? And to him as the president of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, I'm interested in a couple of specific points in this letter. First, in the first paragraph we read: "In the new situation on the territory of the Rogatica Municipality, the Crisis Staff of the SDS Municipal Board Rogatica is not able to carry out its decisions due to a group of armed Serbs, headed by a member of the Main Board SDS BiH Rajko Kusic, who was ruthlessly rushing with threats to attack into the town, in case that municipality and the Public Security Station are not unconditionally divided into Serbian and Muslim parts within two hours' time." So my question about that paragraph is simply: What you wrote here is correct, Mr. Kusic was making threats like that in late March 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now the next paragraph begins: "The Crisis Staff, in compliance with your instructions, believes that the factual division on the ground should be and is already there, however the official division must accompanied by laws issued by relevant Serbian Ministries ..." And you conclude that paragraph saving: "We believe it is dangerous to be the originator of the war situation when the Serbian people are not sufficiently prepared and provided." Now, I have three questions about this paragraph. First, when you refer to "your instructions," you are referring to instructions that is SDS in Rogatica received from the SDS Main Board; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so. I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And around when did the Rogatica SDS receive these instructions?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Look, Sveto Veselinovic was the president of the board. I was in charge of the Executive Committee. And as for that meeting in Pale, we were abreast of that. He's the author of that letter, he signed it as the first signatory. I was the last as the president of the Executive Committee. And I was aware of things that he informed us about and me about, but believe me I can't remember when it was, at what period of time, at what month.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We'll have an opportunity to revisit that with another witness. Third, the concern you express about starting a war in this paragraph is that the Serbian people in Rogatica were not yet sufficiently prepared. By "prepared" you meant that in your view, the three of you, they had not been sufficiently armed; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's one thing. Second of all, the mobilisation --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness needs to slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, Witness, again. Okay. Could you please resume. You said, "That's one thing," apparently referring to what you were asked about arming. And then you said, "Second of all, the mobilisation ..." And could you resume from there slowly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. [Interpretation] Absorbed. The mobilisation absorbed a large number of the Serbian military conscripts and took them to the military manoeuvre in Han Pijesak. We were yet a bigger minority without them than we were with them. To launch or embark on a conflict in such a situation would be tantamount to suicide. We did not want that. We resigned. We told them to replace us with other people if they so wanted because we could not be in charge of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, it was around that time, late March 1992, that you helped organise the Gucevo company of the Serb Territorial Defence in Rogatica; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 65 ter 31325.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31325 receives number P6823, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 31353.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, I want to turn now to the agreement that you've discussed to divide the territory of Rogatica between Muslim and Serb parts. You confirmed earlier that was on the 2nd of May 1992. Now, it was your understanding that in a division of the municipality there would be no Muslims in the parts given to Serbs; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we couldn't do that because, for example, in one village there were ten Muslim houses and 15 Serb houses and such a village with more of the houses of one ethnicity would be considered a village of that ethnicity. We did not want to expel anybody out of such a village.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm asking --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I apologise to the court officer but I'm going to need to call up a different document now, 65 ter 31410, page 14.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, this will be your testimony in the Karadzic case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm looking at the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You were asked about the division and you were looking at a map.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This begins at line 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the transcript is only in English so I'll read it to you and I'll attempt to do so slowly.

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And Mr. Karadzic asked you: "If the municipality was divided into two parts, were the Serbs going to be given urban parts and would it be similar to the map that we are looking at?" And you answered -- and it's not the map that I'm interested in for the moment, you answered: "Probably not because it is obvious that this northern line indicates a Serbian neighbourhood, and there is no doubt that in any kind of division there would be no Muslims." So your testimony in the Karadzic case was at least for some neighbourhoods that was going to be placed in the Serbian part, there would be no Muslims after the division; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct. But those were a hundred per cent Serb neighbourhoods without a Muslim house, without a single Muslim, and those neighbourhoods were never a subject of this division because it was well known who those parts would belong to. There were also pure Muslim areas like Zepa. Again, there were no talks about any divisions there because it was already a pure Muslim area. The only subject of talks about divisions were those area where population was mixed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, sir, I'd put it to you that you were asked in the Karadzic case about the division and you gave the answer that I've recited, and so to say that answer applied only to neighbourhoods that were not really part of the division, as you've suggested now, I'd put to you that is a change in your evidence. It is not consistent with your previous testimony. Do you have any comment on that?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is consistent with my previous evidence. When it comes to the division, we stated from the outset that whatever was a majority Muslim population would --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness needs to slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, Witness, could you please resume from where you said, but more slowly: "... we stated from the outset that whatever was a majority Muslim population would ..." And would you resume from there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where a Muslim population was a majority, those areas were not a subject of any talks or negotiations about a division. Such areas would be given to either of the two sides. Where there were Serb settlements or Serb neighbourhoods with a majority Serb population, those areas were also not a subject of negotiations. Only those areas where population was mixed, those areas were a subject of negotiations as to how to divide, how to split such areas with mixed populations.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, I'd like to look at the negotiations a little bit more now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And if we could have back 65 ter 31353.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, I'm --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since we were able to look at the evidence and sometimes look one page further down and one page further up, could we have a look at the next page. Witness, I read to you which part of your testimony in relation to the same. Where you said: "These were predominantly Muslim parts, and of course Serbs had no place there either." Predominantly is not the same as purely. Apparently if there was a predominant Muslim part, you said there was no place for Serbs, and by using the word "either," apparently you also express here that in predominantly Serb parts that Muslims had no place there, which is not exactly the same as what you told us a minute ago. Do you have any comment or any explanation for what I put to you as part of your testimony in the Karadzic case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, gladly. This is what I'm talking about. If a settlement or an area had 55 or 60 Muslim houses, and let's say 30 Serb houses, in any kind of division that settlement or area would be given to the Muslim side and would become part of the Muslim municipality, and the Serbs who found themselves there had to respect the authorities of that municipality and vice versa. If there was a settlement with 60 Serb houses and 15 Muslim house, that territory would be given under the control of the Serbian municipality of Rogatica. And all the minority ethnicities should respect the authority of the municipality that they were given to. That was the division that I had in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now the text suggests otherwise. You didn't say these were predominantly Muslim parts and of course Serbs had to obey to Muslim rule, but you say, "and of course Serbs had no place there ..." which is something quite different from what you told us a minute ago. Any comment or explanation for that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It may have been a play on words. We were talking about a division of the territory into Serb and Muslim municipalities, and obviously you could not draw any borders for each of the ethnicity and for each of the house and every village to be surrounded by a border and then the area would end up looking like a tiger skin. Our logic was that wherever there was a majority population of one ethnicity --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, this does not further serve as an explanation because I was focusing on the words "Serbs had no place there," and in the other situation "Muslims had no place in Serb areas." Mr. Traldi, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 31353.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And this will be a record of an interview you gave to the Rogatica police on the 6th of June 2004.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'd ask for page 3 in both languages, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now at the top of the page in English you explain what happened following the division of the territory. You say: "Both Assemblies separately accepted the division of territory and that was verified during the joint Assemblies Session."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And where is it in the B/C/S? Otherwise the witness will have difficulties to follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Actually, I'm not certain and would need a moment. I apologise, Your Honour. Could we have, please, the previous page in the B/C/S. I think we're looking at the middle of the page now. There are discussions of Sjemec which is what indicates that to me. And we'll see Sjemec mentioned in the third line of the English. And I apologise again, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I be of assistance?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Have you found where it reads in your own language: "Both Assemblies separately accepted the division of territory ..." Did you find that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now after it says that, you told the police: "This was followed by the Serbian Assembly Session at Sjemec attended by all the members of the parties within the Assembly. I was informed that the session was going to take place that day at Sjemec and I went there but I was surprised by an agenda of the meeting. Since the first item on the agenda was appointment of the President of the Executive Committee. This appear since a bit absurd to me since I was the president of the Executive Committee ..." Now a couple of lines later, you mention Milorad Sokolovic was elected as the new president. You say he was elected "with explanation that I was too soft and too accommodating in negotiations and that someone more rough should be appointed." Now, were you telling the truth to the Rogatica police when you said this in 2004?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, wherever I provided a statement in any shape or form, I made sure to tell the truth like I am doing here now. And, yes, I did tell the truth then.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Okay. So I have a couple of questions about what we've just looked at. First, who explained to you that someone more rough should be appointed?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody individually. Nobody at all. But as a group they did tell me. I was tolerant during negotiations, I was reasonable and sensible. I wanted us to divide rather than to wage a war. I did not insist on things that I had to get at all costs. I showed tolerance. I suppose that Mr. Milorad Sokolovic, who was a more experienced politician, was a more skillful negotiator and therefore tougher. His position would have been different than mine because I had never been a politician, not an active politician that is, and in that part they said that I should be removed and that I should be replaced by him. That's how it went.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Who was present at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A tough question. All the Serb members of the assembly. Mile Cajkovic [phoen] was taking the minutes, he was the secretary of the assembly. The president of the Assembly Tomislav Batinic chaired the meeting. Behind my back there was Miroslav Mirkovic, he was one of those who took this statement from me. He was an MP at the time. I don't have a list of the attendees but this is more or less who was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, maybe I can shorten the question. You've mentioned all the Serb members of the assembly was present. Was there anyone else present?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If my memory serves me right, the secretary of the assembly was in charge of the minutes. There were also MPs. But nobody else attended the meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I just ask a question, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: MPs, is that others or is that not others in your understanding Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think witness's understanding is perhaps more relevant than mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, when you say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but in order to understand the question. "Any others," any members of the assembly, are MPs members of the assembly should be explored.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I would need to ask the witness a question in order to answer the question. And Your Honour, Judge Moloto, I think has one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Maybe just answer Judge Orie first.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, when you say MPs do you mean members of the Serb assembly in Rogatica or members of a different assembly?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I meant primarily deputies in the Serb assembly of Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Ujic, you mentioned that no one individually explained to you that you are too soft and Mr. Milorad Sokolovic was rough. You said it was a whole group. Who composed this group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it's a long story. I have to really shorten it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, don't. Don't tell me a story. Just give me the names of the members of the group. That's all.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tomislav Batinic was in the group. He was the president of the municipality. Rajko Kusic, member of the SDS Main Board. The late Veljko Bojovic as a member of the Crisis Staff. And I think Dusan Planojevic who was also a member of the Crisis Staff if I remember correctly. That was the group. And I was told that by this group immediately before I entered the assembly hall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I have one additional question. In response to a question put to you, you said, "There were also MPs ..." when asked about anyone else than assembly members. What did you mean by MPs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This included legally elected deputies from all Serbian political parties who took part in the election and who made up the Serbian Assembly of Rogatica. Those who won the majority in the elections won seats in the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Does that mean that no MPs, that means at the -- at the level of Bosnia-Herzegovina or Republika Srpska were present, that exclusively elected members of the municipal board or the municipal assembly were present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, when I said those were only deputies of the Serbian municipality of Rogatica, no one else came from any other levels of authorities, that's what I meant. There was no one from republic organs of governance. It consisted only of the local deputies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That was the composition. And no one else was present either, even perhaps not a member.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. I can guarantee that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Witness. Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 65 ter 31353.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31353 receives number P6824, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the Chamber has received evidence --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I refer to P6773.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- that about two weeks after this on the 18th of May the Serb assembly withdrew from the agreement to divide Rogatica and claimed the entire territory of the former Rogatica as a Serbian municipality. That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So you mention the agreement in your statement. You've mentioned it in your testimony. At transcript page 12 today, you said: "We tried hard to have an ever-lasting peace until sometime around the 21st of May." So what I'd put to you is that in fact before the 21st, the Serb assembly had withdrawn from the negotiations, withdrawn from the agreement, and claimed the entire territory, and that you have not provided that information which you know to the Trial Chamber in your statement. That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I made a mistake or misspoke, it was not intentional, just an oversight. When we discuss the division of territory into Serbian and Muslim parts, that was in peacetime before a single bullet had been fired, and this was our starting point and in that way we maintained some sort of semblance of peace in Rogatica. However, the first killing that took place on the 6th of May, then the next one on the 20th of May, already disrupted the atmosphere of negotiations and you couldn't call it peace any longer. Any agreement reached before that fell through. So if -- if you are not honouring the agreement, we are going to withdraw from the agreement, and we'll go to the territory --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not understand the last sentence that the witness said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you repeat the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So if they started killing people and disrupted this kind of peace, we withdrew because there can be no negotiations in wartime. And we said, yes, we are going to withdraw and the whole territory belongs to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you also told us a while ago that you are not aware of any -- or that at least there may have been casualties at the other side as well but you just don't know about it. You now give an explanation saying they started killing people, therefore we had to withdraw, whereas you told us that you do not know whether a similar thing happened on the other side which would shed a different light on your decision to withdraw, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That shouldn't be the case. I said that I knew about those killed on the Serbian side. The first one happened the 6th of May while the negotiations were still underway, and I said I don't know about any casualties on the Muslim side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I want to turn now briefly to your military responsibilities. Now, your military service in 1992 you've told us began in the Gucevo Company of the Rogatica Serb TO. That TO then became the Rogatica Brigade of the VRS, right?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not correct. That was a TO local company which operated in the local commune of Gucevo. Its task was to protect only the population in that specific territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I may have asked in an imprecise way. The Rogatica Serb TO then became the Rogatica Brigade of the VRS; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When the army was established, the TO became a constituent part of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, I want to turn now to your position in this brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P353, page 28 in the English and the B/C/S transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, this is one of General Mladic's notebooks from the war. We see here the date Saturday, 30 May 1992, meeting with unit commanders of the SR Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And turning to page 29 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We see at number 4 Rajko Kusic, commander of newly formed Rogatica Brigade. And below that --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And there is no number 5 in the English, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We see your name, deputy commander. So it's right that by 30 May 1992 the Rogatica Brigade was part of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps and you were the deputy commander; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, according to the date that is so. But I was the chief of the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, and I'm aware that you were -- under the brigade rules, deputy commander is one of the powers associated with being Chief of Staff of the brigade; right? Under brigade rules in the JNA and subsequently the VRS?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, well, everybody had their duties, those in the logistics, myself, and everybody else. So according to our military specialties we were assigned different tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Right. So you were both chief of staff and deputy commander; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your answer, sir.

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that's what you said. But then again, I'm telling you that I was the chief of staff of the brigade. Whether that was equal to a deputy or not, I'm not going to go into that. But I was the chief of staff of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I won't explore it further. I think we can reach agreement with the defence on what the brigade rules say.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, you've seen this particular entry before. You say in paragraph 4 of your statement that you were appointed chief of staff around the 20th of June 1992. In fact, we see you being referred to here as deputy commander almost a month earlier, right? And so you had that authority far long before the 20th of June.

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't mention it in one of my statements that I was appointed chief of staff I think in early May 1992 by the commander. Only later an official appointment came from the superior command. I am not disputing that I was appointed chief of staff of the brigade in the beginning of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As chief of staff, you had the authority to assign tasks to subordinates in accordance with the brigade commander's decisions; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right, but you need to know that I am in the artillery and that I trained them not to fire shells randomly. I was supposed to teach them how to engage military targets, and I was also involved in training.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I was just coming to your artillery involvement. Aside from serving as chief of staff you were also artillery co-ordinator for the brigade; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Initially, yes. At the beginning, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, I have several questions about the brigade. First, the brigade command was located in the Upi Trans facility; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for a period of time. Later on it was at the IKM.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And where was the IKM located?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a command post where some elements of the army remained, whereas the command was relocated either closer or further from the front line depending on the need.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you now about the commanders of some of the units --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, I think you asked something and the witness didn't answer it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Where was the IKM located? That was the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I did answer. After the brigade command was moved, it remained at Upi Trans.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Part of the units remained there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The question was where was the IKM located.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was on the premises of Upi Trans company.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Why didn't you answer that at the first place? Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Believe me, if I would know what the Prosecutor wishes to know, I would give a straight-forward answer. I'm not trying to hide anything. Then from the Upi Trans, the forward command post --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That was exactly what the Prosecutor asked you. Please listen carefully to the questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But before we go on, do we understand therefore that the brigade command never left Upi Trans facility? Is that what you are now saying? Because when the Prosecutor said to you, "The command brigade was located in the Upi Trans facility?" You said: "Yes, for a time, but later it went to the IKM." Now, you're saying it stayed at the Upi Trans facility. It never moved to the IKM. Is that how we must understand your evidence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, Your Honours, I was misunderstood. Let me repeat. Initially or for a period of time the brigade command was in Upi Trans. Later as the war operations progressed, the brigade command moved to other locations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: My question then was where -- what location did they move to? That was the question by the Prosecutor. Can you answer that now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can. To the company called DP Jasna in Rogatica. It's a factory that manufactured children's clothes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's a much better answer, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you, sir, now --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- about the commanders of some of the units under the command of the brigade. The commander of the 1st Infantry Battalion was Stojan Perkovic; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, there was a battalion based at Borike that was commanded by Milovan Lelek until he replaced you as chief of staff; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, there was an intervention platoon at Upi Trans, Milenko Jankovic was the commander of that intervention platoon; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, there was also a unit based in Kozici. The commander of that unit in 1992 was Dragoje Paunovic, aka Spiro; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Spiro, right, that's this execution that we talked about.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: What was the title of that unit in the brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was called the 3rd or the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't understand what the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sorry, could you repeat your answer, sir.

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether it was called the 3rd or the Kozici Battalion, something like that. I'm not sure. I think that at first it was called Kozici Battalion and then it was renamed the 3rd.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now turning to another topic, you testified in the Karadzic case that you were aware that two members of the Rogatica Brigade were disciplined for killing a non-Serb; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And they received one-month prison sentences; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was correct. That was the --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- punishment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- you testified as well that you didn't not know of any other cases where members of the Rogatica Brigade were disciplined for committing crimes against non-Serbs; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that some of them were in prison. Whether anyone else was punished for murder apart from the one that I mentioned, you have to believe me that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Okay. And the one that you mentioned when you say that, you refer to the same one as in the Karadzic case, two persons sent to prison for a month because they killed a person that was a prisoner of war; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, a number of members of the brigade had been prosecuted after the war; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And just to be fair, I think you were continuing to answer my previous question. So I'll re-ask the last one. A number of the members of the brigade have been prosecuted after the war; correct? I see you've nodded but you have to articulate your answer for the record.

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: For instance, a group of Rogatica were arrested and charged for the massacre in the village of Karacici in the month of September 1992 just last month; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. Sorry, the proceedings are still ongoing before the BH court. We don't know the outcome, what it will be. However, I am following this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: When I said it had happened just last month, I wasn't suggesting the proceedings were over, sir. Karacici in 1992 was a Muslim village in southern Rogatica; right? Again --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the answer clearly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is correct. Let me just add one thing -- [In English] Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, could you please look at page 72, lines 2 and 3 and check whether you were correctly recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I was. And perhaps the -- oh, no, I wasn't. You are correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: A group --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: A group of members of the Rogatica brigade were arrested.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And they were arrested, they were not "arrived."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Right. They were arrested. You are far more precise than I am at the moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So, sir, I want to turn now to activities in the Rogatica Serb TO in May of 1992. Now, you've mentioned some actions in which Serbs were killed before the agreement was breached -- or withdrawn from, rather. In fact, before that the Rogatica Serb TO had destroyed groups in Zivaljevici and Medna Luka among other places, right?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And leading up to the 17th of May, 1992, the Rogatica Serb TO was calling on the residents of Muslim villages to surrender their weapons; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And it was communicated to the Muslims that if they did not surrender their weapons, Rogatica would be attacked; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you go to war this becomes a legitimate military target. If --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, Witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- members of the opposing party, armed members are there, that's a military target.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, that wasn't the question. That might be a point of discussion between the parties. You were asked whether it was communicated to the Muslims that if they did not surrender their weapons, that Rogatica would be attacked. Was that communicated to the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's what was said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Traldi, you asked a question and you received a confirming answer from the witness about the Rogatica Serb TO destroying groups in Zivaljevici, the expression "to destroy a group" is not entirely clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, when you agreed that the Rogatica Serb TO had destroyed groups in Zivaljevici and Medna Luka, what did you mean by "destroyed"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Destroyed was used by you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sorry, what did you mean to be agreeing to?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was far from my perception and my direct knowledge. That happened in Borik, both Luka and Zivaljevici. The 2nd Battalion was there. It was their area of responsibility. I third -- heard about this destruction but I don't know any details.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, when you used the word "destroy" what did you mean to convey to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: What I meant was to convey information contained in a specific document emanating from the brigade. So if I could, Your Honour, ask --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, when you said that you heard about this destruction, did you hear enemy groups had been killed? I see you've nodded, but you have to articulate your answer for the record.

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. I heard about it. I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, around this time, and I'm speaking now of around the 17th of May, the 18th of May, what the agreement was withdrawn from, the Rogatica forces, Serb forces, were carrying out reconnaissance; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution have 65 ter 31405.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And while we're waiting for that, could the witness tell us about when he heard about this destruction of groups including killing. When did you hear about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Possibly the same day or the following day, a day later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm asking you this because I earlier asked you whether you were aware of any Muslim casualties during that period of time in which you described Serb victims. And I think you said it was on the other side, you didn't know about that. That was therefore not the full truth, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was a minor oversight then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I specifically asked you and you explained why you wouldn't know that, because it was on the other side, you had no information. If you wish, I would read it to you, as a matter of fact, what you said there. I'm just trying to find it in the transcript at this moment. If anyone could assist me, I'm trying to find the ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Mr. President -- I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll read to you again the question and your answer. The question was: "Now you described in some detail about Serbs being killed early May, I think the last incident you mentioned was the 24th, you gave names, et cetera. During that period of time, were only some Serbs murdered or were there also killings committed against Muslims?" Your answer was the following: "Well, believe me, as much as I would like to tell the truth, I knew about those Serb victims because that was in our territory. As for the losses in the Muslim territory, that's something I wasn't able to see. Therefore, I wouldn't like to say anything. Even if there was a single victim, it's a victim." That was your answer. I put it to you that this was not the whole truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, believe me, it was an oversight. It was only when the Prosecutor put his question to me that my memory was jogged and I remembered those days and I remembered those things. However, before the question was put to me, I really, really could not remember those things. I am not denying that I learned about that thing happening, but it was later, later, later, later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I asked you earlier when you learned about it. You said most likely the same day it happened. You were talking about the 17th of May. Is that also an oversight?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dates, dates, dates. Dates will bury me. They are the bane of my life. Believe me, even if I did know something, I did not have that information first-hand. I would hear things from other people a day later, two days later, three days later, so when I mention a date I really cannot guarantee that things happened on those days. The information was sparse.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is beside the point. You said that you learned about it most likely on the same day it happened. I didn't ask you to further say what date that was. And apparently there are good reasons to believe that it happened on the 17th of May, but if there is any doubt about that then we'd -- I would like to -- I would like to warn you that if you are giving testimony which is not in accordance with the truth and if you would do so intentionally, that you expose yourself to prosecution or investigation. Now you explained to us that it was not intentional, but your explanations shows also some inconsistencies including that you did not have the information first-hand. I never asked you about whether it was first-hand information or not but whether you learned about it. Let's leave it to that. Please be careful to give precise answers which present the whole truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I have a follow-up question. Sir, a few minutes ago you were asked about a case of the killings which has resulted into a case that is currently being heard. You answered that, yes, you are aware of it, and you are following the case. You remember that? You said the case is not finished yet but you are following it. You remember that piece of evidence you gave a few minutes ago?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So you did know and you do -- you do -- you are following a case currently which you know involved people who were killed during the war.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, please do.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Believe me, I learned about that only when that group was arrested about a month ago, for example.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: When you learned about it about a month ago, this means that in fact this morning when you were asked the question about people dieing on the Muslim side, you already knew it about a month ago.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I thought you were asking me about the beginning of May 1992. That's why I answered the way I did. As the war went on, obviously there were killings on both sides. And that case also happened during the war. And I only learned about those cases when people were either arrested or declared suspects. I claim with full responsibility that I didn't know. It is not that I had already known and that I don't want to talk about it here in the courtroom. No. I only learnt that when those people were arrested. Before that, I didn't know about the case. I don't even know what year it took place -- or rather, I didn't know before they were arrested.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And in all fairness to the witness, I, re-reading my question, I do see that I focused my question on killings early May, and I mentioned the 24th of May as the last date of the incident described.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I was talking about the killings that Mr. -- the Prosecutor is referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it may be time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is time for a break. We are beyond that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If I might make one brief submission while the witness is exiting, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you think we need him for it and if it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When he's exiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's fine. You may follow the usher, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And that was simply, Mr. President, to clarify any ambiguity in the record. I had not intended to submit 17 May was the date of the destruction of enemy groups. I would submit that date can be located in Exhibit P3924, page 2. I'd intended, when I'd referred to the 17th, 18th, and 19th, to direct the witness's attention to the time-period for my next question. And just in case there was any ambiguity on the record, I wanted to clarify it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which apparently you had a certain event on your mind. Could -- could you tell us what date you'd link to that event?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And it's -- Your Honour, it's the 6th of May for the destruction of a group in Zivaljevici --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the 8th -- I should say both of them are identified in the record as sabotage groups. The 8th are -- [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They are all within the time-limit I used when putting my question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So in that respect, the witness could not have been confused.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Only it would be me that could have been confused.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I would say rather that it was only my statement that needed to be clarified and not anyone else's.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. We take a break and we will resume at 10 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're waiting for the witness to be escorted into the courtroom. Meanwhile, Mr. Lukic, you certainly are aware that there was a reminder by the Chamber staff about reporting on the expert reports of Defence experts. We didn't receive a monthly report which in itself is already worrying, but we expect then that as was expressed in this e-mail to receive your report by Monday. Could we expect such a report on Monday?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, you can, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Traldi, if you would use any document in the near future, perhaps you could already indicate which one it would be so that everyone is in.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think it's already on my screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's already there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It's 65 ter 31405.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, shortly before the break you confirmed that around the 17th of May 1992, the Rogatica Serb TO carried out reconnaissance. What we see here is a report on the reconnaissance carried out in the region of Okruglo and Satorovici. It says it's submitted by Radislav Ljubinac. Now, he was a member of the Rogatica Serb TO; correct? I see you've nodded, but again you have to articulate your answer for the record.

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was a member of the Serbian TO in Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The witness is nodding while the translation is continuing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I apologize.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And therefore just wait until the end of the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you. I had misunderstood.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So, sir, my only question about this document is these are, in fact, two of the villages where the Rogatica Serb TO was carrying out reconnaissance at this time on or about the 19th of May 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were loyal Muslim villages. The villages were there all the time throughout the war, so the answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And could the Prosecution have 65 ter 31406.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: While it comes up, you confirmed Mr. Ljubinac was a member of the Serbian TO. He later became a member of the VRS Rogatica Brigade; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is a report by a Zoran Bojat and it's a report on reconnaissance in the area of Sjemec. Is that another of the areas where reconnaissance was being carried out on or about the 19th of May 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is the area from Borike to Visegradi. It's a hill top around Sjemec with the villages --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Which the witness needs to repeat the names of.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can you repeat the names of the villages you mentioned at the end of your answer, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stavanj, Sjemec, Sjemecko Polje, Medna Luka, Kopito, and further on in the direction of Visegrad along the slope in terrain.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, it says in the second sentence general mobilisation was carried out in the mentioned area. Now mobilisation of Serbs in Rogatica was carried out on or around the 19th of May; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, one could say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 65 ter 31405 and 31406.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31405 receives number P6825. And document 31406 receives number P6826, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6825 and P6826 are admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the results of reconnaissance in Rogatica were reported up to the SRK command; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First to the brigade command and then the amalgamating report was sent to the corps command by the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And just to be very specific, the results of reconnaissance in Rogatica on or around the 19th of May were reported up to the brigade command and then to the corps command; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But the title is incorrect. It was a summary of all the reports and a report summarised like that was then sent to the corps command.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can the Prosecution please have Exhibit P352, page 349 in English and 357 in B/C/S transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, looking back to the 17th of May, 1992, what we are going to see here is another one of General Mladic's notebooks from during the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Talking about the notebooks. You earlier said at a page you showed to us that there was no 5. You remember that?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. As a matter of fact, there is a mis -- there seems to be a mistranscription or translation, it says "May" where it's in a series of one, two, three, four, five, six -- seven, apparently "five" is understood as a reference to a month and is translated by "May", which is -- and it was the 30th of May, but I don't think that -- if you look at the original, both B/C/S handwritten and the other one, it becomes clear that there is a clear transcription or translation error there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We don't intend to rely on the word "May" in that portion --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We can request anything the Chamber wants, but for the record --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- we don't intend to rely on the word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, in general terms, there's no need to correct it for the proceedings here because it has not sufficient relevance, but perhaps for the basic materials it's good to have it as accurate as possible. But I leave that in your hands. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So, sir, we see here in the middle of the page in both languages a meeting 17 May 1992, Sokolac, 1200 hours. And General Mladic is recording talks with representatives of Rogatica, Olovo, Han Pijesak, Pale, and the Belgrade people from this area. Did you attend this meeting?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this doesn't tell me whether I was there or not and I am not familiar with this meeting, so I don't know whether I was there or not. Perhaps I was but I don't know for a fact. Therefore, I would refrain from answering either yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, turning to page 354 in the English and 362 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: General Mladic is recording tasks, and we see at point 1, he writes: "Monitor the situation at the front gathering as much data about the enemy." And at point 3 he writes: "Speed up mobilisation and bring RJ," that's war units, "up to strength." Sir, we've seen that in the next couple of days reconnaissance and mobilisation were carried out by Serb forces in Rogatica municipality. Were instructions given or tasks defined at this meeting passed on to you to pass on to the soldiers under your command?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw these assignments in a written form. I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, can the Prosecution please have 65 ter 31404.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for me to understand the answer. When you said "I didn't," did you mean to say that you did not pass on any instructions you had received to the soldiers under your command? Is that how we have to understand it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I did not see these instructions and therefore I could not forward them to anybody because I didn't see them. I didn't receive them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But that wasn't the question. The question was not whether you had seen this written instructions but whether instructions were given or tasks defined that were passed on to you. That does not necessarily include that you would have seen those instructions. Did you receive any instructions which may relate to what we just read as having been discussed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, believe me. I don't remember that I ever received them or that I ever saw them, but I do agree that there were mobilisation calls. There was an ongoing mobilisation at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let me ask two questions to follow-up on that. First, you've confirmed reconnaissance and mobilisation were undertaken. Who instructed that Serbs -- that Serb TO units conduct reconnaissance on or about the 18th and 19th of May 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The staff commander of the Serbian TO, Mr. Rajko Kusic. He was the one who could have done that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And were you aware that he'd issued such instructions?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whatever I say, I might be wrong. But believe me, I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is -- what we see here is an order from the SRK command to the Rogatica Brigade TO command, dated the 22nd of May 1992. And it reads here: "Pursuant to the orders of superior command, and to ensure the most effective possible realisation of the organisational and establishment changes in the Corps and better organised operations by units in the zone of responsibility. "I hereby order. "Strengthen the former TO units of the defence forces of the Serbian Republic of BH and form the following."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And if we could turn to page 2 in both languages, point J.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And it says: "Form the Rogatica Territorial Defence from the territory of Rogatica. The brigade commander will be Bogdan Kusic." Should that read Rajko Kusic?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bogdan Kusic did not exist. It has to be Rajko Kusic. This is a typo or a translation mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And so on the 22nd of May your -- would the Rogatica Serb TO, the Rogatica Brigade of the VRS, your brigade, was receiving orders from the SRK command; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE UJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It makes sense, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 65 ter 31404.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31404 receives number P6827, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I see the time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Witness, we are not able to conclude your testimony today and since we are not sitting tomorrow we would like to see you back on Monday, but I want to instruct you that you should not speak or communicate with anyone about your testimony, whether that is testimony already given or still to be given on Monday. If that is clear to you, you may follow the usher and we would like to see you back Monday morning at 9.30 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day and we'll resume Monday, the 20th of October, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 20th day of October, 2014, at 9.30 a.m.
